Article Title: Cummins, Starc, Hazlewood and priceless lessons: Abhishek Moond and Vasudev Prasad Singh soak in Australia's fast-bowling culture
Article Text:
(L-R) Vasudev Prasad Singh, Pat Cummins and Abhishek Moond at the Allan Border Field in Brisbane (Photo Courtesy: Cricket Australia)

New Delhi:

Sir, yakeen nahi ho raha Cummins (Pat),

Hazlewood

(Josh) aur Starc (Mitchell) ke saath run-up mark kiye hain

Vasu hails from Bihar and Abhishek from Rajasthan. They come from smaller cities in our country. To train with Cummins, Starc and Hazlewood is something they would not have imagined even in their wildest dreams. M. Senthilnathan

Bihar's Vasudev Prasad Singh in the nets at the Allan Border Field in Brisbane. (Cricket Australia)

For someone who has bowled most of his formative years on matting wickets, this was an experience he will never forget. Ashok Kumar | Coach Vasudev Prasad Singh

Abhishek Moond (centre) with Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc during the training session at the Allan Border Field in Brisbane. (Cricket Australia)

Emerging pacers Abhishek Moond and Vasudev Prasad Singh visited Australia alongside former India fast bowler Tinu Yohannan and MRF Pace Foundation Program Manager and Head Coach M. Senthilnathan for a two-week high-performance program. (Cricket Australia)

Vasudev Prasad Singh (center) with Australian pacers Josh Hazlewood (left) and Mitchell Starc (right). (Cricket Australia)

Vasudev Prasad Singh and Abhishek Moond trained alongside Australia's Test squad for two weeks as part of the long-running partnership between the MRF Pace Foundation and Cricket Australia. (Cricket Australia)

(I can't believe I have marked my run-up alongside Hazlewood and Starc)," Ashok Kumar recalled the first conversation he had with his ward, Vasudev Prasad Singh, from Brisbane on July 14.Singh, 20, from Bihar's Muzaffarpur district, and 18-year-old Abhishek Moond from Rajasthan's Sikar district trained alongside Australia's Test squad for two weeks as part of the long-running partnership between the MRF Pace Foundation and Cricket Australia.MRF Pace Foundation Program Manager and Head Coach M. Senthilnathan said watching the two youngsters during the first couple of days was an absolute delight."They were like kids in a candy store, pinching each other. They were overwhelmed for the first two days," Senthilnathan told TimesofIndia.com from Brisbane."Vasu hails from Bihar and Abhishek from Rajasthan. They come from smaller cities in our country. To train with Cummins, Starc and Hazlewood is something they would not have imagined even in their wildest dreams. But having said that, it was a great learning curve for them.They rubbed shoulders with two of the world's best. They saw how they train, how they bowl in the nets and, most importantly, how they understand and manage their bodies, which is very important for every fast bowler," he added.The duo trained from July 13 to July 24 at Cricket Australia's National Cricket Centre (NCC) in Brisbane. They also attended training sessions involving the Australian men's Test squad at the Allan Border Field."Getting the opportunity to train with the Australian senior team has been an incredible experience," Moond told this website."The whole environment is different. The batters are of the highest quality, so you have to be consistent and keep bowling in the right areas. I've learned that I need to pitch the ball slightly fuller than my usual back-of-a-length."The bounce and movement have been excellent, and the experience has been fantastic. Training with players of this calibre is a huge confidence booster. At my age, getting the chance to practise alongside cricketers I've watched since childhood is very special. I'm sure I'll learn a lot from them."Like Moond, Vasudev Prasad Singh believes the experience extends far beyond simply sharing the nets with Australia's Test stars. For him, the opportunity is about learning the finer aspects of fast bowling in conditions that reward pace and discipline."The biggest advantage of this tour is the opportunity to train with the Australian senior team. We get to learn so much from them. The environment here is excellent, and the conditions are ideal for fast bowling," said Vasudev Prasad Singh."We're able to bowl long spells, which helps us improve our skills. Exposure like this is extremely important for a cricketer. Bowling to world-class batters in favourable conditions teaches you where to bowl, how to plan your spells and how to set the field."Ashok Kumar, a former Bihar cricketer who has worked with the likes of Sakib Hussain and Mohammad Izhar, two other promising pacers from the state, shared an interesting story about his ward."For someone who has bowled most of his formative years on matting wickets, this was an experience he will never forget. Vasu has represented Bihar at the Under-19 and Under-23 levels and has all the attributes to play for India. He has a very good outswing. He is still raw but will be a ready product in a couple of years," Ashok said.Senthilnathan echoed Kumar's sentiments."They are good boys. Their work ethic is excellent. They train hard. They are still raw, but they will only get better from here," he said.The visit is part of a high-performance exchange program that has connected Indian and Australian cricket for more than three decades, making it one of the sport's longest-running international development partnerships.The MRF Pace Foundation and Cricket Australia have worked together since 1992, building on Australian pace legend Dennis Lillee's association with the Foundation after it was established in Chennai in 1987.The program gives young Indian cricketers exposure to Australian conditions and training methods, while Australian players sharpen their skills in subcontinental conditions. The partnership has helped shape several leading fast bowlers. Australian greats Glenn McGrath, Mitchell Johnson and Brett Lee have all been associated with the Foundation, while Indian stars such as Javagal Srinath and Zaheer Khan are among those who benefited from its development pathway.Looking ahead, Senthilnathan believes the Brisbane stint will prove to be a defining chapter in the youngsters' development."We've had a long association with Cricket Australia and it has helped so many Indian pacers over the years. We saw what Prafull Hinje and Sakib Hussain did after their exposure here. Prafull spent three weeks training in Brisbane and returned a different bowler. Experiences like these accelerate growth. Vasu and Abhishek are still raw, but they have the attitude and work ethic to go a long way. You'll see them making an impact in the years to come," he said.
Article Summary: Vasudev Prasad Singh and Abhishek Moond trained alongside Australia's Test squad for two weeks as part of the long-running partnership between the MRF Pace Foundation and Cricket Australia. The duo trained from July 13 to July 24 at Cricket Australia's National Cricket Centre in Brisbane.

Article Title: Sports is the central pillar of India's development agenda
Article Text:
Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya (ANI Photo)

The Khelo India mission sets a clear and ambitious goal: India must emerge as one of the world’s top 10 sporting nations by 2036 and break into the top five by 2047. By aligning these milestones with the Viksit Bharat vision and the centenary of Independence, the mission elevates sport beyond the pursuit of medals, positioning it as a central pillar of India’s national development agenda.The Union Budget’s 18% increase in sports spending for FY 2026-27, compared with the new 10-year Khelo India mission, reinforces that shift. It frames a future Olympic bid not as an isolated sporting aspiration, but as a statement of India’s economic confidence, institutional maturity, and nation-building ambitions.A case in point: The recent shift in budget momentum that saw the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports allocation rise by 18% to Rs 4,479.88 crore for 2026-27 (from a revised Rs 3,346.54 crore in 2025-26) was one of the sharpest year-on-year jumps in the ministry’s history.At a time when unemployment continues to be a larger subject of discussion across the country’s public and private sectors, this governmentpushed thought-bubble around development of the sports sector in the coming decade certainly has a larger connotation. Investing in sport simultaneously addresses youth engagement, employment generation, health and fitness, while nurturing a new economy sector.Deloitte-Google’s “Think Sports” report projects India’s sports market at US$130 billion by 2030, growing at 14% CAGR — nearly double India’s GDP growth rate.The same report projects 10.5 million jobs and US$21 billion in indirect tax revenue by 2030.From the above budget allocation, the Sports Authority of India will receive Rs 917.38 crore, the National Sports Federations (NSFs) Rs 425 crore, and Khelo India itself Rs 924.35 crore — spread across training centres, coaching, sports science and grassroots competitions (Khel Mahakumbhs).Where cricket is concerned, the sport broke all its past barriers in these recent five years, bringing close to Rs 4,600 crore to the table through the initiation of Women’s Premier League (WPL) – a first of its kind T20 league for women that stood on the pillars of gender equality and equal pay.The IPL, through sale of media rights – where internet rights went past the traditional television rights value to create a record-breaking revenue cycle – underlined the larger idea of Digital Bharat.However, cricket aside, it is the non-cricketing space where the tide has really been turning, even if gradually.While dedicated sports-only Private Equity data – especially outside of cricket – remains thin and fragmented, the broader Indian PE and venture capital activity remains deep, giving sports-adjacent sectors (technology, infrastructure, media, D2C sportswear, apparel) a large domestic capital pool to draw from.Privately run sports leagues like kabaddi, football, volleyball, table tennis and hockey are building independent sponsorship and merchandise streams, reducing — even if only marginally — cricket’s near-total share of commercial revenue, underlining future potential.Sustained double-digit growth compounds quickly. With the sports economy projected to grow at 13–14% annually — comfortably ahead of nominal GDP growth — the sector is steadily becoming a more meaningful contributor to India’s economy. India already exports 60% of the sporting goods it manufactures, with the sector employing close to half a million people directly.Any flipsides to the narrative? The northern sectors across Jalandhar (Punjab) and Meerut (UP) alone account for 75 to 80% of national production. And while it represents the idea of a cluster-economy story, it is also a concentration risk worth flagging to make way for a diversification opportunity.Technology and artificial intelligence represent another major opportunity. The space is projected to go past the US$1b Indian market by 2030 at a 19% CAGR, if the DeloitteGoogle report is to go by, covering fan-engagement platforms, performance analytics and broadcast automation.The country’s existing strengths in software and analytics are already a shot in the arm for export of sports-tech services, a practice the cricket industry has begun to embrace already. Here, the government’s broader AI mission further carries a five-year outlay of a billion dollars (approx. Rs 10,300 cr) that can push forward newer initiatives.Last but not the least, is the focus on modern-day sports infrastructure. The growing need to promote sport across the length and breadth of the country for various reasons is only going to accelerate infrastructure growth.The 2030 Commonwealth Games could do a lot more to Ahmedabad than what the 1982 Asiad and the 2010 Commonwealth Games did to New Delhi, where infrastructure growth is concerned. In Mumbai, the Maharashtra government’s clarion call to have more stadiums on the outskirts of the city. The state of Odisha’s remarkable progress in sports and sporting infrastructure over the last decade.The alarming rate at which private investors are eyeing sports infrastructure growth for business opportunities around the country – can all be potential catalysts serving a larger thought.The Indian sports economy, at this point, is a swirling ocean. It is time to adjust the sails and move forward.
Article Summary: The Khelo India mission sets a clear and ambitious goal: India must emerge as one of the world’s top 10 sporting nations by 2036 and break into the top five by 2047. Investing in sport simultaneously addresses youth engagement, employment generation, health and fitness, while nurturing a new economy sector. The sports economy is projected to grow at 13–14% annually.

Article Title: Gold for Esha Singh; Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker claims bronze at Shooting World Cup in Hangzhou
Article Text:
Gold for Esha Singh (in the middle) and Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker (on the right) claims bronze

NEW DELHI: Esha Singh struck gold for India at the ISSF World Cup in Hangzhou on Monday, winning the women's 25m pistol title in a commanding display, while two-time Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker added a bronze to complete a memorable outing for the country.The victory marked India's first gold medal of the ongoing World Cup and further strengthened its campaign in Hangzhou. Esha, who set the world record in the event earlier this year, lived up to her billing by topping the podium with a score of 40 out of 50 in the final.The 21-year-old stayed in control throughout the contest, finishing three points clear of China's Yueyue Zhang, who claimed silver with 37. Esha consistently found her rhythm across both stages of the final before pulling away in the elimination rounds to seal an emphatic win.Manu Bhaker also returned to the podium after securing bronze in the same event.The Indian shooter edged past North Korea's Hyon Gyong Pak in a tense double shoot-off to finish third with 28 points, ensuring India had two medal winners in the women's 25m pistol competition.Esha's latest triumph continues an impressive season for the Hyderabad shooter, who rewrote the world record during the ISSF World Cup in Munich earlier this year.She has now added another major international title to her growing list of achievements.The double podium finish also boosted India's overall medal tally in Hangzhou to three. Earlier in the competition, Sainyam had won silver in the women's 10m air pistol event.With Esha's gold and the two silver and bronze medals, India climbed to second place in the medal standings, behind hosts China, who continue to lead the table with 14 medals, including six gold.
Article Summary: Esha Singh wins women's 25m pistol title at ISSF World Cup in Hangzhou. Two-time Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker claims bronze in the same event. India climb to second place in the medal standings behind hosts China.

Article Title: 'Want him to improve his overall fitness': VVS Laxman identifies key area for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
Article Text:
India's Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (ANI Photo)

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's dazzling performances against Zimbabwe have earned widespread praise, but stand-in India head coach VVS Laxman believes the teenage sensation still has an important area to develop if he is to fulfil his enormous potential.The 15-year-old capped off an outstanding series with a brilliant 81 off 49 balls in the third T20I in Harare, guiding India to a 35-run victory and a 3-0 clean sweep. His 151 runs across three matches made him the leading run-scorer of the series and earned him his first Player of the Series award.While Sooryavanshi's fearless stroke play has already made him one of India's brightest young prospects, Laxman said improving his overall fitness would be crucial for the youngster's long-term growth."The one area we want him to improve is his overall fitness," Laxman said.The former India batter also highlighted Sooryavanshi's commitment and desire to contribute to the team, pointing to an incident during the third T20I when the teenager wanted to continue despite suffering an injury while attempting a diving catch at deep square leg."He's a very young boy. He himself wants to get better in every aspect of the game.Even today, when he got injured (while attempting a diving catch running in from deep square leg), he still wanted to stay on the field. It was our physio who asked him to come off. That's the eagerness and earnestness he has to contribute in every possible way to the team," he added.Laxman has closely monitored Sooryavanshi's development over the past year through his role as the BCCI's Head of Cricket. The youngster flourished under his guidance during India's victorious ICC Men's Under-19 Cricket World Cup campaign earlier this year, finishing as the tournament's highest run-scorer with 439 runs and being named Player of the Tournament.The Zimbabwe series was another significant step in Sooryavanshi's rapid rise. Having already impressed during his two seasons with the Rajasthan Royals in the Indian Premier League, the left-handed opener once again showcased his ability on the international stage, underlining why he is regarded as one of the country's most exciting batting talents.Despite the accolades, Laxman's message was clear: refining his fitness levels will be a vital part of Sooryavanshi's journey as he looks to build on an already impressive start to his career.
Article Summary: India head coach VVS Laxman says Vaibhav Sooryavanshi needs to improve his fitness. The 15-year-old was the leading run-scorer in the 3-0 T20I series win against Zimbabwe. Sooryvanshi scored 151 runs across three matches and was named Player of the Series.

Article Title: BCB, BCCI working on September window, subject to government nod; Afghanistan T20Is may be postponed
Article Text:
Bangladesh's Towhid Hridoy plays a shot during the Asia Cup cricket match between India and Bangladesh (AP Photo)

New Delhi:

In a development which could bring about a thaw in the relationship between the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) and the Indian cricket board ( BCCI ) after a year’s uncertainty, TOI understands that both boards are working on an itinerary for India’s tour of Bangladesh in the first half of Sept.It has been learnt that the BCCI is set to push back the thre-match T20I series against Afghanistan to be held in Delhi to clear a window for a white-ball series in Bangladesh. The eventual nod for the series will come from the Indian govt, but the boards want to make sure everything is ready when the approval comes.India refused to tour Bangladesh last year due to diplomatic tensions which was followed by Bangladesh forfeiting their place in the T20 World Cup in India after Mustafizur Rahman was ousted from the IPL in Jan.TOI understands that the BCB has kept all its venues free from Sept 1 as it is proposing a few combinations for BCCI to choose as per convenience. India’s Test tour of Sri Lanka is due to end on Aug 27. If the series against Afghanistan is pushed back, that could open up a two-week window in Sept. The Afghanistan series, to be hosted by Afghanistan Cricket Board, was scheduled to start from Sept 13.“BCB is also fine with the idea of holding all matches at one venue.They ideally prefer three T20Is at one venue and three ODIs in another. Dhaka and Chattogram are the leading venues. Playing just one format was a possibility too. The two boards held discussions on the sidelines of the recent ICC meet in London. India’s commitment to Afghanistan is a hurdle that was discussed. But the tour is subject to govt approval,” a BCCI source told TOI.The BCCI had informed the selectors about the Afghanistan series, but an official announcement of Afghanistan hosting India in Delhi was delayed for this reason. It is now learnt that preparations for that series have been pushed back. IPL chairman Arun Dhumal, answering to a query on the relationship with Bangladesh post the Mustafizur episode, had told TOI in May that the BCCI has decided to move on from the bygones and the board intends to build healthy relationships with other member boards.
Article Summary: India refused to tour Bangladesh last year due to diplomatic tensions. Bangladesh forfeited their place in the T20 World Cup in India after Mustafizur Rahman was ousted from the IPL in Jan. India’s Test tour of Sri Lanka is due to end on Aug 27. If the series against Afghanistan is pushed back, that could open up a two-week window.

Article Title: Yash Dayal set to join Chhattisgarh, seeks NOC from UPCA
Article Text:
Royal Challengers Bengaluru's Yash Dayal (PTI Photo)

Lucknow: Uttar Pradesh pacer Yash Dayal has sought a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Uttar Pradesh Cricket Association (UPCA) to switch to Chhattisgarh for the upcoming domestic season.Speculation was rife that Dayal would feature in the UPT20 League after playing in the Ghaziabad Premier League in June, where he took nine wickets in four matches. However, the left-arm pacer has decided to move on.Yash represented Uttar Pradesh from 2018 to 2025, playing 27 first-class matches and taking 84 wickets. In List A cricket, he claimed 36 wickets in 23 matches, while in T20s, he picked up 66 wickets in 71 matches.Talking to TOI, Dayal said, "I have applied to the UPCA for an NOC. From next month, I will join the Chhattisgarh team's fitness camp and play for Chhattisgarh in the upcoming domestic season."The left-arm pacer revealed that talks with the Chhattisgarh Cricket Association had been underway even before the start of the season, but he initially needed time to make a decision. After discussions with his seniors and family, he decided to go ahead with the move.Dayal said leaving Uttar Pradesh was an emotional and difficult decision, as the UPCA had played a major role in his career."Playing for the UP team and representing Uttar Pradesh in the Ranji Trophy has been extremely special and a matter of pride for me. The UP Cricket Association is very close to my heart. UP gave me recognition. I played in the IPL and was also selected for the Indian team. The UPCA has contributed immensely to whatever I have achieved," he said.Speaking about the difficult phase he has faced recently, including legal and mental challenges, Dayal said cricket helped him stay strong and focus on making a comeback."As a cricketer, no one wants to go through a phase that shakes his life. But cricket has taught me how to make a comeback and perform in every situation. I did not run away from difficulties. My family and my coaches always stood by me," he said."Many times I felt like giving up because, despite being capable, I was not able to play. In such circumstances, sometimes the mind starts to break," he added.The pacer also clarified his situation with Royal Challengers Bengaluru, saying the franchise had not dropped him. He said he remained part of the squad but was not travelling with the team during the season.On the ongoing legal matters, Dayal confirmed that he had been granted bail in both cases and that the proceedings were still underway. "In both cases, I have officially been granted bail and the cases are still under process," he said.Meanwhile, a senior UPCA official told TOI, "Yash has applied for an NOC, and his request is still under consideration."
Article Summary: Yash Dayal has applied for a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Uttar Pradesh Cricket Association. The left-arm pacer will join the Chhattisgarh team's fitness camp next month. Dayal confirmed that he had been granted bail in both cases and that the proceedings were still underway.

Article Title: CWG 2026: Indian boxers unfazed by baggage snag on arrival
Article Text:
Santiago Nieva (Image credit: X)

India’s boxing contingent arrived in Glasgow confident after a productive two-week multinational training camp in Belfast, but its final preparations were briefly disrupted when some boxers’ luggage failed to arrive ahead of Thursday’s opening ceremony.The 14-member squad travelled from Belfast to Glasgow on Tuesday after completing the intensive camp, during which the boxers benefitted from quality sparring and competition-specific training. However, several athletes were left without their bags, which also contained their ceremonial outfits, TOI has learnt.Sources said officials from the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) and the chef-de-mission’s office were at the airport on Wednesday, coordinating with the airline to ensure the baggage reached the contingent before the ceremony. The boxing competition begins on Friday and runs until Aug 1.The incident, however, has not gone down well with the Boxing Federation of India (BFI). Sources said that after the issue surfaced, the federation asked the boxers to submit declarations stating that they would not speak to the media about internal team matters and would instead remain focused on their performances.Despite the logistical hiccup, the mood in the camp remains upbeat. “We are settling in well in Glasgow. We had a good camp in Belfast where everybody got quality sparring and proper preparations. The boxers are managing their weights well. We will have the draws soon. We are coming with high expectations for this competition,” India women’s head coach Santiago Nieva told TOI .India’s 14-member squad features Olympic bronze medallist Lovlina Borgohain and Jaismine Lamboria, the world No. 1 in the women’s 57kg category.
Article Summary: India’s boxing contingent arrived in Glasgow confident after a productive two- week multinational training camp in Belfast. The 14-member squad travelled from Belfast to Glasgow on Tuesday after completing the intensive camp. Several athletes were left without their bags, which also contained their ceremonial outfits, TOI has learnt.

Article Title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi makes a statement as India sweeps T20I series against Zimbabwe
Article Text:
India's batsman Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (AP Photo/Wonder Mashura)

It was the shot of the series by a 15-year-old batter who looks set to light up the game for the next quarter of a century. Seeing Vaibhav Sooryavanshi shimmy down the track, Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza cleverly dragged his length back. However, the teenage sensation adjusted superbly to launch the ball a staggering 102 metres over wide long-on for a six. The delivery wasn’t in his arc or ideal hitting zone, but the left-hander had already made up his mind to clobber it.After three ordinary outings against England, Sooryavanshi has made a statement on India’s tour of Zimbabwe, heralding a new chapter in his fledgling career. On Sunday, the precociously talented youngster smashed 81 off 49 balls, studded with eight fours and four sixes, to propel India, who opted to bat first at the Harare Sports Club, to 192 for five in the third and final T20I — a dead rubber. Zimbabwe finished on 157 for seven. Mayank Yadav claimed three for 29 in four overs to finish with five wickets at 14.40.With five overs remaining, Sooryavanshi needed 19 more runs for his maiden international hundred. But Brad Evans produced a brilliant diving catch after sprinting in from long-off to dismiss him off Wessly Madhevere. Sooryavanshi signed off as the series’ leading runscorer with 151 runs at 50.33 and a phenomenal strike rate of 196.10.Brief Scores: India: 192/5 (V Sooryavanshi 81; B Evans 2/41) beat Zimbabwe: 157/7 (Ryan Buri 54 not out; Mayank Yadav 3/29, Yash Thakur 2/45).
Article Summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi smashed 81 off 49 balls, studded with eight fours and four sixes. India, who opted to bat first at the Harare Sports Club, to 192 for five in the third and final T20I. Zimbabwe finished on 157 for seven.

Article Title: WI vs PAK 1st Test: Former captain Shan Masood's unbeaten 88 helps Pakistan recover against West Indies on Day 2
Article Text:
Pakistan's Shan Masood. (Photo by AP/PTI)

NEW DELHI: Pakistan ended Day 2 of the first Test against West Indies in a strong position, reaching 199/3 in reply to the hosts' first-innings total of 311.Former captain Shan Masood led the fightback with an unbeaten 88, making an impressive return with the bat after recently stepping down from the captaincy. He was well supported by Imam-ul-Haq, who scored 63 as the pair shared a crucial 155-run partnership.Pakistan lost an early wicket when Azan Awais was bowled by Kemar Roach , but Masood and Imam steadied the innings with positive strokeplay.Masood brought up his half-century in just 46 balls, while Imam reached his 11th Test fifty before being dismissed for 63. New captain Babar Azam added 23 before falling late in the day, while Salman Agha remained unbeaten at stumps alongside Masood after bad light brought play to an early close.Earlier, West Indies were bowled out for 311 after resuming the day at 194/3. Shai Hope top-scored with 92, narrowly missing out on a century, while Kavem Hodge made 84.Hope anchored the innings despite losing partners regularly and received useful contributions from Shamar Joseph, who scored a quick 23.Pakistan's bowlers pulled things back after West Indies' solid start. Mohammad Ali picked up four wickets, while Mohammad Abbas claimed three after making an immediate impact with the second new ball.Khurram Shahzad also struck early to remove Hodge, helping Pakistan wrap up the innings before their batters took control through Masood and Imam.
Article Summary: Pakistan reach 199/3 at stumps on Day 2 of first Test against West Indies. Shan Masood unbeaten on 88, while Imam-ul-Haq scored 63. West Indies were bowled out for 311 after resuming the day at 194/3.

Article Title: Commonwealth Games: IOA issues health advisory amid Glasgow chill
Article Text:
Indian contingent pose as they arrive for the opening ceremony of the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games (PTI Photo)

New Delhi :

With Glasgow hit by a sudden spell of cold, cloudy and rain-soaked weather, the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) and the country’s chef-de-mission office have advised athletes to take preventive measures to minimise the risk of upper respiratory and airborne infections during the Commonwealth Games.Sources told TOI that athletes have been verbally briefed at their respective hotels, with officials urging them to avoid unnecessary outdoor exposure, dress warmly and wear face masks while travelling or in crowded indoor spaces. Frequent hand washing has also been recommended as an added precaution.The advisory comes after temperatures dropped sharply over the past two days, making conditions considerably colder, especially during the evenings. A few Indian athletes have reported mild cold symptoms, including runny noses, but none has required hospitalisation.Officials stressed there is no cause for alarm, while underlining the importance of preventive care with several medal events still to come. “It is quite cold and cloudy here,” Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra said, reflecting the challenging weather conditions athletes have encountered in Glasgow.
Article Summary: Athletes advised to take preventive measures to minimise the risk of upper respiratory and airborne infections during the Commonwealth Games. A few Indian athletes have reported mild cold symptoms, including runny noses, but none has required hospitalisation. “It is quite cold and cloudy here,” Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra said.

Article Title: 'It hurts when you can't give back': Abhishek Sharma breaks silence after nightmare Zimbabwe tour
Article Text:
India's batsman Abhishek Sharma (AP Photo)

Abhishek Sharma Insta post

India completed a 3-0 T20I series sweep over Zimbabwe, with Vaibhav Sooryavanshi dominating the headlines after the 15-year-old became the youngest player ever to win the Player of the Series award in men's international cricket.Sooryavanshi announced himself with a blistering 50 off just 18 balls in the first T20I, followed it up with 20 off nine deliveries in the second match, and capped off the series with a superb 81 off 49 balls in the third and final T20I.However, the success Sooryavanshi enjoyed was in stark contrast to that of his opening partner, Abhishek Sharma . The left-hander endured a disastrous series against Zimbabwe, managing scores of 1, 8 and 2.His struggles extend beyond the Zimbabwe tour. Across India's recent T20I assignments in the UK against Ireland and England, and the Zimbabwe series, Abhishek managed just one half-century. In his last six T20Is for India, he has registered scores of 10, 16, 3, 1, 8 and 2, highlighting a worrying dip in form.Following the series, Abhishek took to Instagram to express his disappointment."It hurts when you can't give back what so many people believe you're capable of.But this game always rewards those who keep showing up. Happy that the team got the win. Will be back stronger."With Sooryavanshi's rapid rise, Abhishek is likely to feel the pressure. Sanju Samson , despite being India's Player of the Tournament during their T20 World Cup triumph, is still waiting for a place in the playing XI, making competition for opening spots even more intense.India's next T20I assignment is at the Asian Games in September, followed by a home series against the West Indies in October, giving Abhishek more than two months to address his shortcomings. For now, the only way forward is to put his head down, go back to the drawing board and rediscover the form that made him one of India's most exciting T20 batters.
Article Summary: India completed a 3-0 T20I series sweep over Zimbabwe. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi became the youngest player ever to win the Player of the Series award in men's international cricket. Abhishek Sharma managed scores of 1, 8 and 2 in the series.

Article Title: 'He understands, assesses and gets better': VVS Laxman reveals what makes Vaibhav Sooryavanshi so special
Article Text:
India's Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (AP Photo)

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's remarkable start to international cricket continued to draw praise, with India interim head coach VVS Laxman highlighting the teenager's maturity and willingness to learn after his composed innings in the third T20I against Zimbabwe.The 15-year-old anchored India's batting effort with a well-crafted 81 off 49 deliveries in Harare, hitting eight fours and four sixes to guide the visitors to 192/5. India went on to register a 35-run victory, completing a clean sweep of the three-match series. Sooryavanshi finished as both Player of the Match and Player of the Series after scoring 151 runs across the three games.Unlike his explosive fifty in the opening T20I, Sooryavanshi had to alter his approach in the series finale.Batting on a used surface where the ball gripped and came slowly onto the bat, the left-hander paced his innings smartly. He reached his fifty in 31 balls before lifting the scoring rate to finish with a strike rate of 165.30.Speaking after the match, Laxman said the youngster's biggest strength was his ability to constantly evaluate his performances and improve with every opportunity."Very mature. And that's what I really appreciate about Vaibhav . With each and every experience, each and every match, he understands, he assesses, and he gets better," Laxman said."So I think he does a lot of review of each and every practice session. Not only match."Laxman pointed out that the conditions in Harare demanded a different batting approach and praised Sooryavanshi for recognising what the situation required instead of sticking to his natural attacking game."So today what you saw was a mature innings. Because it was a used wicket. The wicket which we played the match on yesterday. So the ball was stopping and coming. The wicket was slow," Laxman said.The former India batter also revealed that Zimbabwe had prepared specific plans to restrict the young opener after his impact earlier in the series, but Sooryavanshi responded impressively."And I thought today the Zimbabweans bowled well. Had a plan to him. So he countered that plan. And it was a very, very mature knock from Vaibhav."The innings showcased another side of Sooryavanshi's game. After blasting a 19-ball half-century in the series opener, the teenager demonstrated that he could also build an innings according to the demands of the conditions. His ability to shift gears and overcome Zimbabwe's bowling plans added another dimension to an already impressive start to his international career.
Article Summary: India beat Zimbabwe by 35 runs in the third T20I in Harare. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scored 81 off 49 deliveries to guide India to 192/5. The 15-year-old was named Player of the Match and Series. India won the three-match series 2-1.

Article Title: 'Special moment': Shreyas Iyer after maiden T20I series win as India captain
Article Text:
Photo/BCCI

India captain Shreyas Iyer credited the team's fearless approach and the maturity of its young players after leading India to a 3-0 T20I series sweep over Zimbabwe, calling his first series win as captain a "special moment. "India completed the clean sweep with a 35-run victory in the third and final T20I at the Harare Sports Club on Sunday. After posting 192/5, the visitors restricted Zimbabwe to 157/7.Speaking after the match, Iyer praised the energy and intent shown by the players throughout the series."As we saw how fearless they are, they are a young bunch of players who have been showing tremendous energy on the field and the intent, especially when you play back-to-back games.To have such kind of energy is what I require as a captain and as a team, and they could deliver today as well, back-to-back games. So, yeah, a special feeling for me to win the series over here in Zimbabwe. Clinical, 3-0. So it's going to be a special moment," Iyer said during the post-match presentation.When asked about his role as one of the senior players in the squad, Iyer said several teammates already had plenty of experience and that his job was to help them stay relaxed."I think if you see the record, I've played almost a similar amount of matches compared to all of them, which is around 55 to 60. So, I mean, experience-wise, there are many players who have tremendous experience because nowadays they play in the IPL as well," he said."So, yeah, they are special talent and the best you could get out of them, it's beneficial for the team as well. So every time I step onto the field, I see to it that how I can make sure that they are comfortable and relaxed because that's when you can get the best out of them," he added.India's batting was led by 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who scored 81 off 49 balls with eight fours and four sixes. Ishan Kishan made 29, Iyer scored 27 off 18 balls, and Rinku Singh added 25 off 14 deliveries to help India reach 192/5.Zimbabwe's chase never gained momentum after Yash Thakur dismissed Brian Bennett with the first ball of the innings before removing Dion Myers and Sikandar Raza in his opening spell. Mayank Yadav finished with 3/29, while Ravi Bishnoi and Ashok Sharma took one wicket each. Ryan Burl remained unbeaten on 54, but Zimbabwe fell 35 runs short.
Article Summary: India completed the clean sweep with a 35-run victory in the third and final T20I at the Harare Sports Club on Sunday. After posting 192/5, the visitors restricted Zimbabwe to 157/7. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 15, scored 81 off 49 balls with eight fours and four sixes.

Article Title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi shines as India return to winning ways with 3-0 sweep over Zimbabwe after England and Ireland setbacks
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi

India completed a 3-0 series sweep over Zimbabwe with a 35-run win in the third and final T20I in Harare on Sunday, thanks to Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's 81 and a disciplined bowling effort led by Mayank Yadav.The series victory also marked a turnaround for India after losing their previous two T20I series against England (0-4) and Ireland (0-2).Defending 193 on a slow pitch, India restricted Zimbabwe to 157/7 despite an unbeaten 54 from Ryan Burl.Zimbabwe once again lost early wickets and could not make good use of the powerplay. Yash Thakur (2/45) removed Dion Myers and captain Sikandar Raza off successive deliveries in the fourth over, reducing the hosts to 34/3.Earlier, Mayank Yadav (3/29) gave India the perfect start by dismissing Brian Bennett with the first ball of the innings. Bowling with pace and accuracy, Mayank kept Zimbabwe under pressure throughout.India also dropped four catches and leaked a couple of boundaries in another below-par fielding display.Burl tried to revive the chase with a 60-run partnership for the fifth wicket with Wesley Madhevere (28), but Zimbabwe had already lost too many wickets to stay in the contest.Earlier, India also suffered an early setback after choosing to bat, losing Abhishek Sharma for 2. The left-hander edged Blessing Muzarabani to wicketkeeper Tadi Marumani, extending his poor run in T20Is. Abhishek's last six scores now read: 10, 16, 3, 1, 8 and 2, dating back to the third T20I against England in Nottingham last month.Sooryavanshi, however, adapted well to the conditions. The 15-year-old paced his innings carefully on the slow Harare Sports Club surface. He scored just 11 runs from his first 10 balls and added 15 more in the next 10 deliveries before bringing up his second T20I fifty in 31 balls.The Bihar batter still produced some eye-catching shots. He drove Brad Evans through the straight boundary off a yorker and later hit Sikandar Raza for a 102-metre six. He also played a reverse sweep for four against Wesley Madhevere. Overall, it was a controlled innings from the teenager.Sooryavanshi added 75 runs for the second wicket with Ishan Kishan (29) before sharing another 50-run stand with captain Shreyas Iyer (27).He missed out on a century when Brad Evans took a catch at long-off off Madhevere's bowling.After the dismissals of Sooryavanshi and Shreyas, India's middle order could not score quickly. The team managed only 47 runs in the final five overs, with Rinku Singh's 25 off 14 balls helping India finish close to the 200-run mark.
Article Summary: India complete a 3-0 series sweep over Zimbabwe with a 35-run win in the third and final T20I in Harare on Sunday. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's 81 and a disciplined bowling effort led by Mayank Yadav helped India to victory.

Article Title: 'My game is the same': Vaibhav Sooryavanshi after winning 'man of the series' at just 15
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (ANI Photo)

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's Series Performance

1st T20I: 50 off 19 balls (18-ball fifty, 4 fours, 4 sixes)

2nd T20I: 20 off 9 balls

3rd T20I: 81 off 49 balls (8 fours, 4 sixes)

'Dream Come True,' Says Sooryavanshi



India beat Zimbabwe by 35 runs

India's teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi announced his arrival on the international stage in emphatic fashion, winning both the Player of the Match and Player of the Series awards after starring in India's 3-0 T20I series sweep over Zimbabwe in Harare.Sooryavanshi finished as India's highest run-scorer in the series with 151 runs in three innings, blending fearless strokeplay with remarkable composure beyond his years. His performances earned him his first-ever international Player of the Match award and maiden Player of the Series honour, a fitting reward after dominating Zimbabwe's bowling attack throughout the series.Speaking after receiving both awards at the post-match presentation, the youngster described the moment as the fulfilment of a lifelong ambition."It felt really good. Our preparation was very good during the two or three days after we arrived in Harare. I also played the Under-19 World Cup here, so I really enjoy playing at this venue, everyone backed me, the captain, the coaches, everyone, so I'm very happy," Sooryvanashi said.Known for his attacking style, Sooryavanshi said he never changed his natural game despite making the step up to international cricket."My game is the same as what I play in T20 cricket. I was just trying to do that for the team. In all three matches, I tried to give the team a good start. If I got a good start, then I wanted to make the innings bigger. That was my only approach. What I do in practice, I try to replicate it in the match as well. Dream come true, my first Player of the Match and Player of the Series!'' Sooryavanshi added.India completed a 3-0 T20I series sweep over Zimbabwe with a convincing 35-run victory in the third and final match at the Harare Sports Club on Sunday. Defending 192, the visitors restricted Zimbabwe to 157/7, handing skipper Shreyas Iyer his first T20I series win since taking over the captaincy.The chase got off to the worst possible start for Zimbabwe as Mayank Yadav dismissed Brian Bennett with the very first ball of the innings. Yash Thakur then struck twice in the fourth over, removing Dion Myers and Sikandar Raza, leaving the hosts reeling.Ryan Burl fought a lone battle with an unbeaten 54 off 43 balls, while Wessly Madhevere contributed 28. However, regular wickets prevented Zimbabwe from threatening India's total. Mayank Yadav finished with 3 wickets, Yash Thakur claimed 2, while Ravi Bishnoi and Ashok Sharma chipped in with one each.Earlier, India posted 192/5 after electing to bat, thanks largely to a sensational 81 off 49 balls from 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. The teenage opener smashed eight fours and four sixes, registering his second T20I half-century before falling 19 runs short of a maiden century.Ishan Kishan scored 29, Shreyas Iyer added 27, and Rinku Singh's unbeaten 25 off 14 balls provided the finishing flourish. For Zimbabwe, Brad Evans was the standout bowler with 2/41.The victory marked India's third successive T20I win, completing a dominant clean sweep after difficult tours of Ireland and England, with Vaibhav Sooryavanshi finishing as the leading run-scorer of the series.
Article Summary: India beat Zimbabwe by 35 runs to complete 3-0 T20I series sweep. Teen sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi wins Player of the Match and Series awards. India posted 192/5 after electing to bat, thanks largely to 81 off 49 balls from 15-year-old.

Article Title: Zimbabwe's Sikandar Raza surpasses Rohit Sharma, Pakistan's Babar Azam in unwanted T20I record after golden duck vs India
Article Text:
Babar Azam, Sikandar Raza

Most ducks as T20I captain (Full Member teams):

8 – Aaron Finch

7 – Sikandar Raza

6 – Babar Azam

6 – Rohit Sharma

Most ducks for Zimbabwe in T20Is:

Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza went past Pakistan's Babar Azam and former India captain Rohit Sharma for the second-most ducks by a captain in T20 internationals during the third and final T20I against India in Harare on Sunday.Raza was dismissed for a golden duck by India pacer Yash Thakur, taking his tally of ducks as T20I captain to seven. Only former Australia captain Aaron Finch has more ducks as captain in the format, with eight. Babar Azam and Rohit Sharma are next on the list with six each.The dismissal came in the fourth over of Zimbabwe's chase of 193. Yash bowled a short-of-length delivery that hurried Raza, who attempted to play towards the leg side. The ball took the leading edge and looped back towards the bowler. Yash reacted quickly, moved to his left in his follow-through and completed a one-handed catch to dismiss the Zimbabwe captain. The wicket also put the Indian pacer on a hat-trick.The duck also saw Raza move level with former Zimbabwe wicketkeeper-batter Regis Chakabva for the most ducks by a Zimbabwe player in T20 internationals.Earlier, India posted 192/5 after being asked to bat first.Fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi led the innings with 81 off 48 balls. He paced his innings according to the conditions on a pitch that offered some help to the bowlers and brought up his second T20I fifty in 31 balls.The youngster produced some of his trademark shots, including a straight drive for four off Brad Evans' yorker and a 102-metre six off Raza. He also played a reverse sweep for four against Wesley Madhevere before eventually finishing with 81.
Article Summary: Sikandar Raza was dismissed for a golden duck by India pacer Yash Thakur. Raza's duck took his tally of ducks as T20I captain to seven. Babar Azam and Rohit Sharma are next on the list with six each.

Article Title: Mayank Yadav equals Bhuvneshwar Kumar's T20I Record with first-ball wicket against Zimbabwe

Mayank Yadav has done it again. the pacer struck with the very first ball of Zimbabwe's innings, dismissing Brian Bennett for a golden duck in the 3rd T20I, repeating the feat he produced in the series opener.Bowling at 147kph, Mayank delivered a sharp short-of-a-length ball that nipped away off the surface and climbed awkwardly. Bennett, caught on the back foot while attempting to defend, could only edge the ball towards first slip, where Vaibhav Sooryavanshi showed brilliant reflexes to complete a sharp chest-high catch to his left. Mayank immediately leapt into the air and celebrated with a trademark roar after claiming yet another first-ball wicket.With the dismissal, Mayank Yadav equalled Bhuvneshwar Kumar 's Indian record of taking a wicket with the first ball of a T20I innings three times. Mayank had first reached the milestone in the opening T 20I on July 23, when he marked his return from a two-year injury layoff.

Article Title: Tejas Shirse, Sarvesh Kushare headline India’s opening-day athletics challenge
Article Text:
Sarvesh Kushare (left) and Tejas Shirse

Tejas Shirse will be looking to open India’s medal account in athletics as the track and field events begin at ther Glasgow Commonwealth Games on Monday. Shirse had broken the men’s 110m hurdles national record with a time of 13.27s during Indian Athletics Series in Ludhiana last month, and has carried that form into the season after winning gold at Inter-State Athletics Championships in Bhubaneswar.He had also claimed the Federation Cup title in Ranchi and will be hoping for a strong showing in his maiden Commonwealth Games. However, all this still feels like a dream considering he was sidelined for more than four months after suffering a serious right ankle injury late last year.“To be honest, 13.27 wasn’t even part of the plan. Even qualifying for Commonwealth Games wasn’t something we were thinking about initially. But things worked out and I was able to achieve both,” Shirse had said after his victory in Bhubaneswar.The injury marked one of the lowest points of his career, something he wrote about in detail in an Instagram post in March that began with the words, “I hate it!” The period was so difficult that, at times, he went days without sleeping and was “angry and frustrated to the point of snapping.”“People kept talking about my ‘potential’, and I started hating that word because everyone said I had so much potential, yet I wasn’t able to show it,” he said.Shirse, however, kept believing in himself and, with the support of his team, emerged stronger. “I’ve come out of that phase as a much more mature person. I take every experience positively now,” he said. “Looking back, I’m happy I went through that phase because it changed me.”Besides his physio Nilesh Makwana and coach James Hillier, what helped him most during that period was patience. He believes the experience prepared him for “the battles on the track and in life as well.”He, however, kept much of it away from his family so as not to worry them. His coach, James Hillier, though couldn’t have been prouder of his comeback.“We only resumed track training on April 13, and exactly two months later, on June 13 in Ludhiana, he broke the national record. That’s an extraordinary achievement,” Hillier said. What’s going to be an even bigger achievement is if he makes it to the podium. It’s challenging but Hillier thinks it’s possible.Besides Shirse, the trio of Sarvesh Kushare , Tejaswin Shankar and Aadarsh Ram will look to light up the evening session in the men's high jump final. Kushare heads into CWG on a high after breaking the national record with a leap of 2.31m and is joint fourth on this season's world list. Shankar, meanwhile, won bronze at the previous edition, while Ram has a personal best of 2.27m.In the men’s long jump qualification, Murali Sreeshankar and Lokesh Sathyanathan will be in action, while Gurindervir Singh begins his campaign in the opening round of the men’s 100m. Gurindervir broke the national record in Ranchi with a time of 10.09 seconds and has sounded confident of putting up a good show on his CWG debut.
Article Summary: Shirse had broken the men’s 110m hurdles national record with a time of 13.27s during Indian Athletics Series in Ludhiana last month. He had also claimed the Federation Cup title in Ranchi. Shirse was sidelined for more than four months after suffering a serious right ankle injury late last year.

Article Title: Mirabai Chanu creates history with Commonwealth Games gold hat-trick in Glasgow
Article Text:
Mirabai Chanu (ANI Photo)

There is a gold-winning performance and then there is the Mirabai Chanu way of doing it. In Glasgow on Sunday, the Tokyo Olympics silver medallist lifter made it look like child’s play as she went about completing a hat-trick of Commonwealth Games gold medals. In her very first attempt in the clean and jerk category of the women’s 48kg, Mirabai lifted 105 kg, which was good enough for gold.The 31-year-old battle-hardened Mirabai lifted a total of 190kg, showing that she never faced a threat to the top finish, lifting as she did 22kg more than the silver medallist Ruth Nyong of Nigeria (168kg). The bronze went to Malaysia’s Irene Henry (167kg).Also en route, she lifted 85kg in the snatch to create a new Games record and a new Commonwealth record.“It was a good performance, and it went the way we had planned it. We knew that 105kg would be enough for her in the clean and jerk category so she didn’t take much pressure off lifting more. Our focus is doing well at the Asian Games , so we want to ensure she doesn’t take more load than needed,” Mirabai’s coach Vijay Sharma told TOI.“Although Mirabai made it look very easy, we didn’t take the competition lightly. I am glad that Mira became the only lifter to have won three gold and a silver at the Commonwealth Games,” the coach added.Earlier, another Manipur lifter, Rishikanta Singh, helped India add a silver to its tally. Rishikanta took the second spot in the men’s 60kg competition after lifting 264kg and equalling the Commonwealth record in the snatch category.Rishikanta lifted 121kg in snatch and started the clean and jerk with a successful lift of 143kg in his first attempt. He, however, failed in his bid to lift 148kg and 151kg in the next two attempts, owing to a discomfort in his knee.Rishikanta had entered the clean and jerk category in the lead, along with Malaysia’s Bin Kasdan Mohamad Aniq, who had also lifted 121kg in snatch. The Malaysian went ahead in clean and jerk by lifting 149kg in his first attempt, followed by a successful 152kg lift in the clean and jerk to take his total to a Games record of 273kg.“I came here for gold. After the snatch, I was in the leading position, but my knee created a problem. I was able to clean the weight but could not push because one thigh was not working properly. I tried my best,” Rishikanta told PTI.Kenya’s Joshua Amunga Mboya took bronze with a total lift of 260kg (115kg+145kg).In swimming, the quartet of Dhakshan Shashikumar, Aneesh Sunil Kumar Gowda, Aryan Nehra and Srihari Nataraj clocked 7:39.48 to finish third in their heat and advance to the final of the men’s 4x200m freestyle relay event. The Indians finished behind Australia (7:08.66) and England (7:18.13) in Heat 2.In lawn bowls, Rupa Rani Tirkey and Pinki Singh lost to Namibia to break their streak of three wins in the women’s pairs event. Rupa and Pinki lost the tie-break 0-3 against the pair of Amanda Steenkamp and Diana Viljoen.In boxing, a dominant show by Preeti fetched her a Referee Stops Contest win in the women’s 54kg Round of 16 bout.
Article Summary: Mirabai Chanu lifts 105kg in her first attempt in clean and jerk category of 48kg. The 31-year-old lifts a total of 190kg, 22kg more than the silver medallist Ruth Nyong of Nigeria. The bronze went to Malaysia’s Irene Henry (167kg).

Article Title: Three medals in a day! Raja Muthupandi's silver joins India's Commonwealth Games weightlifting medal spree
Article Text:
Glasgow: India's Raja Muthupandi secures a silver medal during the men's 65kg weightlifting final at the 23rd Commonwealth Games, in Glasgow, Scotland. (PTI Photo/Ravi Choudhary)(PTI07_27_2026_000017B)

Glasgow: Malaysia's gold medallist Muhamad Aznil Bidin, centre, India's silver medallist Raja Muthupandi, left, and Papua New Guinea�s bronze medallist Morea Baru during the men's 65kg weightlifting final at the 23rd Commonwealth Games, in Glasgow, Scotland. (PTI Photo/Ravi Choudhary)(PTI07_27_2026_000023A)

Long road back to the podium

Glasgow: India's Raja Muthupandi competes during the men's 65kg weightlifting final at the 23rd Commonwealth Games, in Glasgow, Scotland. (PTI Photo/Ravi Choudhary)(PTI07_27_2026_000022A)

India's medal tally grows

Raja Muthupandi won the silver medal in the men's 65kg weightlifting event at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, adding another podium finish to India's strong start in the sport.The 26-year-old lifted 126kg in the snatch and 160kg in the clean and jerk for a combined total of 286kg to finish second. Malaysia's Muhamad Aznil Bin Bidin claimed gold with a Commonwealth Games record total of 299kg, while Papua New Guinea's Morea Baru secured bronze with 282kg.The silver was Muthupandi's first Commonwealth Games medal after finishing sixth in the men's 62kg event on his debut at Gold Coast in 2018.Muthupandi's progress was halted by a serious elbow ligament injury in 2019, with the COVID-19 pandemic further disrupting his rehabilitation. After moving up to the 67kg category, he also found opportunities limited as Jeremy Lalrinnunga established himself as India's leading lifter in the division, eventually winning Commonwealth Games gold in Birmingham in 2022.Jeremy's injury struggles and dip in form later reopened the door for Muthupandi, who switched to the 65kg category and rebuilt his place in the national setup.He announced his return by finishing ninth at the 2025 World Championships, setting a personal-best total of 299kg through lifts of 130kg in the snatch and 169kg in the clean and jerk.Muthupandi arrived in Glasgow after winning silver at the 2025 Commonwealth Weightlifting Championships and has now added a Commonwealth Games silver to his résumé.His medal was India's third in weightlifting on the day, following podium finishes by Rishikanta Singh and Mirabai Chanu, and increased the country's overall tally to four medals at the Games, comprising one gold, two silvers and one bronze.
Article Summary: Raja Muthupandi won the silver medal in the men's 65kg weightlifting event at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Malaysia's Muhamad Aznil Bin Bidin claimed gold with a Commonwealth Games record total of 299kg. Papua New Guinea's Morea Baru secured bronze with 282kg. It was India's third medal on the day, following podium finishes by Rishikanta Singh and Mirabai Chanu.

India's Jadumani Singh Mandengbam produced another assured display at the 2026 Commonwealth Games, defeating Pakistan's Sumama Rehman by unanimous decision to book his place in the men's 55kg boxing quarter-finals and keep India's medal hopes alive in the category.The Manipur boxer claimed a dominant 5-0 victory in Sunday's Round of 16 contest in Glasgow, showing control throughout the bout to overcome his Pakistani opponent and move into the last eight.The victory continued Jadumani's impressive run at the Games after he had earlier opened his campaign with a convincing win over Scotland's Aaron Cullen in the Round of 32.Jadumani entered the pre-quarter-final in confident form after producing a one-sided performance against Cullen, while Rehman came into the contest fresh after receiving a bye in the preliminary round.The Indian boxer, who won silver in the 50kg division at last year's World Boxing Cup Finals in Noida before moving up to the 55kg category this season, once again showcased the speed and composure that have made him one of India's leading prospects.He also became the first member of India's boxing contingent to step into the ring at the Glasgow Games.The opening round proved to be the most evenly contested phase of the contest.Both fighters exchanged punches freely, with Rehman making good use of his height and reach advantage while Jadumani relied on quick footwork, sharp movement and fast combinations to score.The judges narrowly favoured the Indian after the first round, but there was little separating the pair as they continued to trade attacks.The pace and intensity increased significantly during the second round.Jadumani gradually established greater control before producing one of the decisive moments of the contest by scoring a knockdown on Rehman, shifting the momentum firmly in his favour.He maintained that advantage through the closing stages of the fight and secured a unanimous verdict after three rounds, with all five judges awarding him the contest.The victory sends Jadumani into the quarter-finals, where he will face England's Ellis Trowbridge on Tuesday for a place in the medal rounds.Under Commonwealth Games boxing rules, both losing semi-finalists receive bronze medals, meaning victory over Trowbridge would move the Indian into the last four and guarantee him a place on the podium.India has sent a 14-member boxing team to Glasgow, consisting of seven male and seven female boxers, with expectations of another strong medal haul.India has already secured its first confirmed boxing medal of the Games through Olympic medallist Lovlina Borgohain Competing in the women's 75kg division, Lovlina received a direct bye into the semi-finals, automatically guaranteeing herself at least a bronze medal because both defeated semi-finalists receive podium finishes under Commonwealth Games regulations.She is scheduled to face Tuvalu's Tarona Khanum Badi Pasoni Taafaki in the semi-finals on July 31, with a place in the gold medal bout at stake.India's boxing campaign has gathered momentum elsewhere in Glasgow as well.Sachin Siwach, one of the country's leading medal hopes in the men's 60kg division, progressed from the Round of 32 after edging Canada's Keoma Al-Ahmadieh by a 4-1 split decision in a closely contested bout.The 26-year-old from Bhiwani, Haryana, will next face England's William Hewitt on Monday with a place in the quarter-finals on the line.With Jadumani safely through to the last eight, Lovlina already assured of a medal and Siwach continuing his campaign, India's boxing contingent remains firmly in contention across multiple weight categories as competition continues in Glasgow.
Article Summary: India's Jadumani Singh Mandengbam defeated Pakistan's Sumama Rehman by unanimous decision to book his place in the men's 55kg boxing quarter-finals. The Manipur boxer claimed a dominant 5-0 victory in Sunday's Round of 16 contest in Glasgow. India has sent a 14-member boxing team to Glasgow, consisting of seven male and seven female boxers.

Article Title: Mirabai Chanu wins India's first gold at Commonwealth Games 2026 with record lift
Article Text:
Mirabai Chanu

Star weightlifter Saikhom Mirabai Chanu gave India its first gold medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games after winning the women's 48kg title in Glasgow on Sunday.The 31-year-old lifted a Commonwealth Games record 85kg in the snatch before registering a Games record 105kg in the clean and jerk. She finished with a total lift of 190kg to claim the gold medal.The victory gave Mirabai her third successive Commonwealth Games gold medal, having also won the title in the 2018 Gold Coast Games and the 2022 Birmingham Games.The Tokyo Olympics silver medallist had earlier won a silver medal at the 2014 Commonwealth Games, which were also held in Glasgow.Mirabai was in control of the competition from start to finish.She finished 22kg ahead of Nigeria's Ruth Asuquo Nyong, who won the silver medal with a total lift of 168kg.Her campaign began with a setback as she failed her opening snatch attempt at 82kg. However, she recovered in her next attempts to post the record-breaking 85kg lift.Having taken an eight-kilogram lead on the clean and jerk as a result of her record-setting snatch, the Manipuri lifter dropped the bar on her first attempt at the clean and jerk, but responded in a champion's manner by lifting 105kg on her second attempt and thus secured the gold medal well before the competition ended.The lift not only secured the gold but also shattered the Commonwealth Games record in the clean and jerk category and bettered the total lift mark.With the title already secured, Mirabai did not attempt her third clean and jerk lift, keeping in mind the Asian Games, which are scheduled to begin in less than two months.
Article Summary: Saikhom Mirabai Chanu won the women's 48kg title in Glasgow. The 31-year-old lifted a Commonwealth Games record 85kg in the snatch. She also registered a Games record 105 kg in the clean and jerk. It was her third successive Commonwealth Games gold.

Article Title: CWG 2026: Neeraj Chopra checks in after long injury rehab
Article Text:

India’s star attraction Neeraj Chopra finally touched down in Glasgow on Saturday morning ahead of a high-stakes men’s javelin throw competition.Sporting an all-black outfit comprising a sweatshirt, track pants and a black cap, Chopra cut a relaxed figure as he made his way into the hotel where the athletics and para-athletics contingent are staying. The Olympic and world champion returns to the CWG after missing the 2022 Birmingham edition because of injury.Gold Coast champion in 2018, Chopra enters Glasgow with just one competition under his belt over the last year. Since finishing a disappointing eighth at the World Championships in Tokyo last Sept while battling a troublesome lower back injury, the 28-year-old has stayed away from competition, focusing entirely on rehabilitation and recovery.His only appearance since then came in the Doha Diamond League, where an 85.69m throw fetched him fourth place.Having also dealt with ankle, shoulder, wrist and adductor issues in recent years, Chopra has taken a cautious approach to his return. “I’m coming from Switzerland. The preparations have been good. After the Doha DL, we increased the intensity of my workouts and fitness regime. It took time to recover from injury issues this time,” Chopra said after arriving in Glasgow.Neeraj will once again renew his rivalry with Pakistan’s Olympic and defending CWG champion Arshad Nadeem, while Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage, who produced a world-leading 92.62m in Rome DL earlier this month, enters the competition as the man in form.
