Article Title: CWG: Jhandu wins bronze as India open Glasgow campaign; Sachin survives tough boxing test
Article Text:
Jhandu Kumar

(WITH INPUTS FROM ARNAB SEAL)

As India slept, Jhandu Kumar hauled the country’s Commonwealth Games campaign onto the medal table.The 28-year-old para powerlifter from Bihar delivered India’s first medal of the Glasgow Games late on Friday, winning bronze in the men’s heavyweight event at the SEC Armadillo. Jhandu finished with 130.9 points after opening with a successful lift of 181kg and improving to 190kg on his second attempt. He then failed to complete 196kg, but his best lift was enough to secure third place.After pressing 190kg, Jhandu sat upright with a smile, thanked God and reached for his wheelchair. His final attempt was agonisingly close, but he could not complete the lift to earn the judges’ approval. He rose smiling nonetheless, though a flicker of disappointment remained as he looked towards his support staff.Jhandu said a technical infringement on the unsuccessful lift had proved costly. “That mistake cost me dearly. Had the lift counted, I would have had a chance to win silver and perhaps even challenge for gold,” he told TOI .Asked whether the occasion had brought additional pressure, Jhandu said, “I had already competed at international events before, so I wasn’t overawed by the occasion. My only focus was to do what I had practised in training and give my best.Small technical mistakes happen in competition, and that’s what happened this time.”In boxing, Sachin Siwach survived a searching test from Canada’s Keoma AlAhmadieh to reach the men’s 60kg round of 16 on Saturday. Al-Ahmadieh troubled the Indian through all three rounds. Sachin, however, landed enough scoring punches to retain a slender edge and secure a 4-1 split-decision victory. He will face England’s Will Hewitt for a place in the quarterfinals on Monday.India’s women endured a difficult Commonwealth Games debut in 3x3 wheelchair basketball, suffering a 16-1 defeat by Wales in their opening Group B match. The Indian team converted only one of its 12 scoring attempts.Lawn bowls, however, supplied another flourish as Rupa Rani Tirkey and Pinki Singh registered their third successive victory in the women’s pairs competition. The Indians edged Tonga’s Paris Baker and Milika Nathan in a tense tie-breaker after the teams split the opening two sets. Rupa and Pinki won the first set 5-2 before Tonga fought back to take the second 6-4. The Indians then prevailed 2-0 in the tiebreaker to remain unbeaten and stay firmly in the race for a semifinal berth.In the men’s singles event, Putul Sonowal suffered his first defeat as he lost 4-8, 8-9 to Malaysia’s Izzat Shameer Dzulkeple in a crucial Section D clash.
Article Summary: Jhandu Kumar wins bronze in men's heavyweight event at the SEC Armadillo. The 28-year-old para powerlifter from Bihar delivered India's first medal of the Glasgow Games. India's women endured a difficult Commonwealth Games debut in 3x3 wheelchair basketball, suffering a 16-1 defeat by Wales.

Article Title: 'He's lying ... isn't sorry at all': Spain's Dani Olmo refuses to accept Argentina assistant coach's 'fake' apology
Article Text:
Spain's Dani Olmo (10) reacts during the World Cup semifinal soccer match between France and Spain in Arlington, Texas, near Dallas, Tuesday, July 14, 2026. (AP Photo/Abbie Parr)

Ayala's explanation prompts response from Olmo

Olmo: 'He's lying'

Diari de Terrassa

Spain want to be remembered for their conduct

Spain's Dani Olmo (10) celebrates with the trophy after the World Cup final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Adam Hunger)

Collective spirit behind Spain's triumph

Spain midfielder Dani Olmo has spoken publicly for the first time about the altercation that followed his side's 2026 FIFA World Cup final victory over Argentina, rejecting Roberto Ayala's apology and accusing the Argentina assistant coach of lying about what triggered the incident.The Barcelona midfielder became one of several Spain players caught up in the chaotic scenes that erupted after the final whistle in New Jersey, where Spain secured their second World Cup title with a 1-0 extra-time victory thanks to Ferran Torres' decisive goal.FIFA has since opened disciplinary proceedings into Argentina's post-match conduct after a confrontation involving several players and members of the coaching staff.The disorder began after Nahuel Molina confronted Spain captain Rodri following the final whistle, with the exchange quickly escalating into a mass altercation involving players and staff from both teams.During the confrontation, television footage showed Argentina assistant coach Roberto Ayala making contact with Olmo as the Spain international stood alongside teammate Eric García.Earlier this week, Ayala acknowledged the incident while insisting it had been misunderstood.Speaking about the confrontation, the former Argentina defender said it had been "more of a shove than a punch" and claimed his reaction came in response to something Olmo had said.Ayala also indicated that he intended to apologise if he met the Spain midfielder in person.Speaking to, Olmo firmly rejected both Ayala's explanation and the apology."Someone who claims to be sorry, but justifies a punch by saying it was a response to a comment, probably isn't sorry at all," Olmo said.The Spain international then directly challenged Ayala's version of events."He's lying, because I didn't say anything to him, so I don't need him to apologise."Rather than focusing solely on the incident itself, Olmo said genuine accountability requires accepting responsibility without attempting to justify what happened."What truly defines us isn't the mistake, but the courage to own up to it with humility, honesty and dignity."His comments directly contradict Ayala's claim that the confrontation was provoked by remarks from the Spanish midfielder.Although the post-match scenes dominated much of the discussion after the final, Olmo said he hopes Spain's World Cup triumph will ultimately be remembered for the way the team conducted itself throughout the tournament."I want people to be proud of how we competed, how we won and, above all, of our behaviour," he said.The 27-year-old also reflected on the wider responsibility carried by elite footballers, particularly given the influence they have on younger supporters."The reach of football means that we players are role models for children and future generations, and that carries a great responsibility."Away from the controversy, Olmo highlighted the values he believes were central to Spain's World Cup-winning campaign."The group, the collective, always above individual players," he said, describing Luis de la Fuente's squad as a close-knit group built on teamwork rather than individual stardom.Olmo also praised the coaching and support staff, stressing that Spain's success was founded on months of meticulous preparation."It's all about hard work, nothing else, to achieve the goal."He explained that preparation extended well beyond training sessions on the pitch."The work isn't just physical. Invisible training is crucial, nutrition, rest, recovery, mental preparation, match analysis and healthy habits."According to Olmo, those elements formed the foundation of Spain's successful campaign, helping the team navigate the demands of the tournament before defeating Argentina to lift the World Cup for the second time in the nation's history.While FIFA's investigation into the post-match incidents remains ongoing, Olmo made clear that he believes Spain's lasting legacy from the tournament should be defined not by the confrontation after the final whistle, but by the football, discipline and collective spirit that carried them to the world title.
Article Summary: Dani Olmo has spoken publicly for the first time about the altercation that followed his side's 2026 FIFA World Cup final victory over Argentina. The Barcelona midfielder became one of several Spain players caught up in the chaotic scenes that erupted after the final whistle in New Jersey. Spain secured their second World Cup title with a 1-0 extra-time victory thanks to Ferran Torres' decisive goal.

Article Title: 'He disappeared': Harry Kane told his Ballon d'Or dream is over despite sensational goal-scoring season
Article Text:
Bayern's Harry Kane reacts after the Champions League opening phase soccer match between Arsenal and Bayern Munich in London, Wednesday, Nov. 26, 2025. (AP Photo/Kin Cheung)

Stellar numbers but major trophies prove decisive





Bayern's Harry Kane celebrates after scoring his side's opening goal during the DFB Pokal, German Cup final soccer match between VfB Stuttgart and Bayern Munich in Berlin, Germany, Saturday, May 23, 2026. (AP Photo/Ebrahim Noroozi)

England's Harry Kane reacts after the World Cup semifinal soccer match between England and Argentina in Atlanta, Wednesday, July 15, 2026. (AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough) CORRECTION: Corrects byline.

Petit believes Kane faded when it mattered most

Spain's World Cup triumph reshapes the race

Spain's Lamine Yamal gestures during a World Cup round of 32 soccer match against Austria in Inglewood, Calif., near Los Angeles, Thursday, July 2, 2026. (AP Photo/Andre Penner)

How the Ballon d'Or is decided

Harry Kane's chances of winning the 2026 Ballon d'Or have suffered a significant setback following England's World Cup campaign, with former France, Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder Emmanuel Petit insisting the Bayern Munich striker is no longer among the leading contenders despite one of the finest individual seasons of his career.Kane entered the Ballon d'Or race as one of the favourites after a prolific campaign for both club and country, but Petit believes his inability to deliver silverware in football's biggest competitions has weakened his case.The England captain enjoyed a sensational season with Bayern Munich, scoring 61 goals in 51 appearances across all competitions.He finished as the Bundesliga's top scorer with 36 league goals, added 14 goals in the UEFA Champions League, 10 in the DFB-Pokal and one in the German Super Cup, helping Bayern secure a domestic league and cup double.However, Bayern fell short in Europe after being eliminated by Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League semi-finals, denying Kane the first Champions League title of his career.His international campaign followed a similar pattern. Kane scored six goals in seven appearances at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, but England's hopes of lifting the trophy ended with a 2-1 semi-final defeat to eventual runners-up Argentina before Thomas Tuchel's side defeated France to finish third.Across club and country, Kane finished the season with an extraordinary return of 73 goals and eight assists in 66 matches, strengthening his position as one of world football's most prolific forwards.Despite those remarkable statistics, Petit believes performances in the biggest matches ultimately carry the greatest weight in Ballon d'Or voting.Speaking to Mr Gamble, the 1998 World Cup winner said Kane's candidacy had been damaged by Bayern's Champions League exit and England's failure to reach the World Cup final."Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or chances are over," Petit said."If you base that only on the German league, okay, no problem at all."But in the Champions League and with the national team, when it started to be really hard to win, I think he disappeared."I can't point the finger at him because he tried everything he could, and he scored many goals, but he didn't have an impact in the big games, just like in the Champions League. So I think there are a few names ahead of him."Petit believes Spain's World Cup victory has significantly altered the Ballon d'Or landscape.The former midfielder highlighted several Spanish stars as leading candidates following their triumph over Argentina in the World Cup final, while also praising Rodri's performances throughout the tournament."Lamine Yamal? He had a great World Cup," Petit said."You know the rules for the Ballon d'Or have changed so much, just like the rules on the pitch. Rodri has been the best player again during this competition. Messi had a great competition, but he plays for Miami."I know the World Cup is above any title you want with your club. But in the meantime, you have to win the title. Is it going to be a Spanish player? I have no idea. But it's going to be tough. And in the end, I hope it won't be a commercial decision."Following Spain's World Cup success, Barcelona teenager Lamine Yamal and Spain captain Rodri have emerged as leading contenders alongside Kane. Lionel Messi remains firmly in the conversation after guiding Argentina to another World Cup final at the age of 39, while France forward Kylian Mbappé enhanced his credentials by finishing as the tournament's Golden Boot winner with 10 goals despite France placing fourth.The Ballon d'Or recognises the world's best male and female footballers based on three principal criteria: individual performances, team achievements and fair play.The men's award is voted on by an international panel of journalists representing the top 100 nations in FIFA's world rankings, while the women's award is decided by journalists from the top 50-ranked countries.Each voter selects 10 players from the official 30-player shortlist, awarding points on a scale of 15, 12, 10, 8, 7, 5, 4, 3, 2 and 1. The player with the highest overall points total wins the award, with the number of first-place votes serving as the first tiebreaker if required.The debate over this year's favourite comes just months after Ousmane Dembélé was crowned the 2025 Men's Ballon d'Or winner, edging out Barcelona teenager Lamine Yamal after a historic season with Paris Saint-Germain.Dembélé led PSG to their first-ever UEFA Champions League title as part of a continental treble, scoring 37 goals and providing 15 assists across all competitions. He also collected the UEFA Champions League Player of the Season award and finished as Ligue 1's top scorer, cementing his status as the standout performer of the previous campaign.The 70th Ballon d'Or ceremony is scheduled to take place in London on October 26, 2026.
Article Summary: Harry Kane's chances of winning the 2026 Ballon d'Or have suffered a significant setback. Former France, Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder Emmanuel Petit insists the Bayern Munich striker is no longer among the leading contenders. Petit believes performances in the biggest matches ultimately carry the greatest weight.

Article Title: Neymar forced to explain himself after viral footage shows him skipping Santos match for poker tournament
Article Text:
Neymar addresses criticism after missing Santos match to attend poker tournament/Image: Instagram

Neymar's Poker footage goes viral

Instagram post fuels debate

Neymar insists he followed Santos' programme

Santos explain why Neymar was rested

as reported by MARCA

Injury frustrations continue after World Cup

Neymar has responded publicly after facing criticism for attending a poker tournament on the same day Santos played in the Copa Sudamericana, using both an Instagram post and a video message to defend himself while insisting his absence from the match had been part of the club's injury-management plan.The Brazil forward, who has endured another injury-disrupted spell since returning to Santos, came under scrutiny after missing his side's 4-1 victory over Universidad Central in the first leg of their Copa Sudamericana play-off before later being seen competing at a poker tournament in São Paulo.Footage later circulated online showing Neymar taking part in the second day of the poker event in São Paulo, further intensifying the debate around his absence from the squad.The images and clips quickly spread across social media, prompting criticism from supporters and Brazilian media questioning his commitment to the club.Neymar has now addressed the controversy directly, while Santos have also explained the reasoning behind his absence.As criticism intensified, Neymar shared a series of photographs from the poker tournament on his official Instagram account.The post showed the 34-year-old seated at one of the gaming tables surrounded by cards and poker chips, accompanied by a brief caption that many interpreted as a response to the backlash."Life is a joke," Neymar wrote.The forward also disabled comments on the post, preventing supporters from replying publicly beneath the images.ID@undefinedCaption not available.The message quickly circulated online, with many viewing it as a pointed reaction to the criticism surrounding his decision to attend the tournament.The former Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain star later addressed the controversy more directly in a video, insisting he had fully complied with the physical programme agreed with Santos."People have come out and just keep talking about the fact that I play poker," Neymar said."I did my morning training. I did not go to the match because I had just started training again. The next day was my day off."The Brazilian explained that his appearance at the poker tournament came only after completing his scheduled training commitments and during an authorised day off.He ended his response with a sarcastic message aimed at those criticising him."Anyway, now I'm preparing for my training. I also want to ask you something: am I allowed to train, or are you going to say something about that as well?"Santos head coach Cuca also defended the club's decision, stressing that Neymar's omission had been carefully planned as part of his recovery from injury rather than any disciplinary or personal issue.According to Cuca, the club's approach was centred on carefully managing the forward's workload following his recent return to training,"Since he was sidelined for a few days and didn't have a holiday, we decided to let him get even stronger, training hard so he could have a run of games," Cuca said."Now, in ten days, we're going to play four matches. What advantage would it be to bring him here? You saw how hard and exhausting the trip is."Cuca added that Neymar remained at the club's training base alongside Willian Arão, João Schmidt and Igor Vinicius, allowing them to continue their physical work ahead of a demanding run of fixtures."That gives us more options for the upcoming games," he said.The latest controversy comes shortly after Neymar's frustrating World Cup campaign with Brazil.After initially raising doubts over his availability, the forward was included in Carlo Ancelotti's squad but a calf injury limited him to just two appearances during the tournament. He scored from the penalty spot before Brazil's World Cup campaign ended with a 2-1 defeat to Norway in the round of 16.Following the tournament, Neymar returned to Santos to continue his rehabilitation before gradually resuming training with the first team.Despite the club's explanation that his absence against Universidad Central formed part of a carefully managed recovery plan, his appearance at the poker event reignited long-standing debates surrounding his off-field decisions.Back at the club where his professional career began, Neymar continues to battle recurring injury problems while remaining one of Brazilian football's most closely scrutinised figures, with his latest social media posts and public defence doing little to quiet the discussion surrounding his priorities away from the pitch.
Article Summary: Neymar has responded to criticism over his decision to attend a poker tournament on the same day Santos played in the Copa Sudamericana. The Brazil forward missed his side's 4-1 victory over Universidad Central in the first leg of their play-off. Footage later circulated online showing Neymar taking part in the second day of the poker event in São Paulo. The images and clips quickly spread across social media, prompting criticism from supporters and Brazilian media questioning his commitment to the club. Neymar has now addressed the controversy directly in a video message.

Article Title: Mexico's next superstar? Gilberto Mora attracts interest from club that made Bellingham and Haaland
Article Text:

Why Dortmund's interest matters

Mora still has plenty of development ahead

Mexico's Gilberto Mora (19) controls the ball against Czechia's David Doudera (21), right, during the World Cup Group A soccer match between Czechia and Mexico in Mexico City, Wednesday, June 24, 2026. (AP Photo/Natacha Pisarenko)

While no formal move has been reported, Dortmund's interest reflects the growing belief across Europe that Mora could become one of the game's next elite young midfielders.Although many supporters first discovered Mora during the World Cup, his rise had already begun long before arriving in North America.The midfielder made his professional debut for Club Tijuana during the 2024 Apertura tournament at just 15 years old before making Liga MX history by becoming the youngest goalscorer ever in Mexico's top flight.Those early achievements established him as one of the country's most exciting prospects, but it was his performances against elite international opposition that significantly elevated his profile.According to MARCA , Dortmund have now begun following Mora's development closely after the tournament, with the German club once again looking toward one of world football's most promising teenage talents.Borussia Dortmund's reputation for developing young players makes any reported interest particularly noteworthy.For years, the Bundesliga club has built its sporting project around identifying exceptional prospects, giving them opportunities at senior level and preparing them for the highest level of European football.Few clubs possess a stronger track record in that area.Jude Bellingham joined Dortmund from Birmingham City as a 17-year-old in 2020 and quickly established himself as one of Europe's finest young midfielders before completing his move to Real Madrid, where he has become one of the club's central figures.Erling Haaland followed a similarly transformative path.After arriving from Red Bull Salzburg, the Norwegian striker exploded into one of football's most feared goalscorers during his time in Germany before earning a move to Manchester City, where he has continued to establish himself among the world's elite forwards.Those success stories have helped cement Dortmund's reputation as one of the best environments in Europe for nurturing elite young talent.Despite the growing attention, Mora's career remains in its early stages.At just 17, he still has significant room for development before reaching the level achieved by players such as Bellingham or Haaland, whose careers flourished after making the move to Dortmund.The reported interest therefore reflects potential rather than an expectation of an immediate transfer.Mexico, meanwhile, will hope Mora continues his progression domestically while attracting further opportunities abroad through consistent performances.His technical ability, confidence in possession and maturity have already marked him out as one of the country's most exciting young footballers.The 2026 World Cup may have introduced Gilberto Mora to millions of supporters around the world, but if Dortmund's reported interest develops into something more concrete, it could prove to be only the beginning of a career following a pathway that has previously helped launch some of football's biggest modern stars.

Borussia Dortmund are said to be monitoring the midfielder's development following his impressive displays on football's biggest stage. Dortmund's interest reflects the growing belief that Mora could become one of the game's next elite young midfielders.

Article Title: Erling Haaland's hilarious one-word verdict after artist's unbelievable mini version of him goes viral
Article Text:
Manchester City's Erling Haaland greets supporters after the Premier League soccer match between Manchester City and Everton in Manchester, England, Saturday, Oct. 18, 2025. (AP Photo/Dave Thompson)

Haaland responds with one-word verdict

The “Nice” trend that has taken over social media

Hours of craftsmanship behind the sculpture

Fans praise artist's remarkable attention to detail

Erling Haaland has reacted after an artist created a remarkably lifelike clay sculpture of the Manchester City and Norway striker, with the finished piece attracting widespread praise online before earning a simple but memorable response from the footballer himself.Fresh from another impressive campaign, including helping Norway reach the World Cup quarter-finals for the first time in their history and finishing the tournament with seven goals, Haaland once again found himself making headlines, this time away from the football pitch.The artwork, created by sculptor Jay the Clay, quickly gained traction across social media after the artist shared a behind-the-scenes video documenting the painstaking process of transforming a block of clay into a detailed miniature version of the Manchester City forward.After the video began circulating online, Haaland himself came across the post and left a brief response in the comments."Nice," the Norwegian striker wrote.The short reply delighted both the artist and thousands of football fans following the project.Anticipating exactly that kind of reaction, Jay had jokingly written alongside the video:"You spend hours on a figure, and then some guy named Erling will comment 'nice'."ID@undefinedCaption not available.That prediction proved remarkably accurate as Haaland acknowledged the work with the one-word endorsement.Haaland’s reaction to the sculpture is part of a growing online pattern that has turned his deadpan, single-word replies into a viral meme of their own.In recent months, the Manchester City striker has become known for leaving minimalist comments—most famously “Nice.” and occasionally “Not nice,” on a wide range of social media posts, from fan edits and highlight reels to unexpected viral clips.The trend has taken on a life of its own across Instagram and TikTok, where users now deliberately tag Haaland in videos ranging from football edits to comedy skits and even music performances, joking that the algorithm has “worked” if “some guy named Erling” shows up in the comments.ID@undefinedCaption not available.What began as a handful of understated reactions has evolved into a running internet joke, with fans actively trying to provoke a response from the striker.Haaland, for his part, has leaned into the humour, continuing to engage with posts in the same minimalist style. His comments have appeared on everything from flute covers of his goal anthem to memes about his own goal celebrations, as well as even personal moments such as his girlfriend’s birthday post.The consistency of the replies has only amplified the trend, turning “Nice” into something of a signature online persona for the Norwegian forward.The viral video showcases every stage of the sculpture's creation, beginning with the construction of the figure's basic frame before gradually building the body and facial features by hand.Jay carefully sculpted Haaland's distinctive hairstyle, facial structure and expression before moving on to finer details that brought the figure to life.The completed sculpture depicts Haaland wearing Manchester City's full home kit, faithfully recreating the club's famous sky-blue colours while also incorporating detailed football boots and accessories.Beyond the uniform, the attention to proportion, posture and facial likeness stood out, with each stage highlighting the patience and precision required to produce such a realistic handcrafted model.The time-lapse format condensed many hours of work into just a few minutes, giving viewers a glimpse into the level of craftsmanship involved without diminishing the effort behind the finished piece.The sculpture quickly attracted significant attention online, receiving more than 110,000 likes as supporters praised both the likeness and the dedication required to complete it.Many comments focused on how accurately the artist had recreated Haaland's appearance, while others applauded the amount of time invested in every small detail, from the facial features to the boots and club kit.For many viewers, the video's appeal extended beyond the finished product itself, with the creative process becoming just as captivating as the sculpture it ultimately produced.Haaland's public acknowledgement only added to the excitement, giving the artist a memorable moment after the project had already resonated with thousands across social media.

Article Title: 'Don't retire yet': Di María makes desperate plea to Lionel Messi after Argentina's World Cup agony
Article Text:
Argentina's Lionel Messi reacts after losing to Spain in the World Cup final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Pamela Smith)

Di María wants Messi to keep playing

Heartbreak in the final does not define Argentina's campaign

Di María also backs Scaloni to continue

Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni leaves the pitch after the World Cup final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Julio Cortez)

Messi yet to reveal his next international decision

Ángel Di María has urged Lionel Messi not to retire from international football following Argentina's heartbreaking defeat to Spain in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final, insisting the captain should continue representing his country for "many more years" despite another painful ending on football's biggest stage.Spain claimed their second men's World Cup title with a 1-0 extra-time victory at the New York New Jersey Stadium after substitute Ferran Torres scored the decisive goal in the 106th minute. The defeat ended Argentina's hopes of retaining the trophy they won in Qatar four years earlier and immediately shifted attention toward Messi's international future.At 39, Messi has yet to confirm whether he intends to continue playing for Argentina.While the 2026 tournament is widely expected to have been his final World Cup, his future beyond that remains uncertain.Di María, who retired from international football after helping Argentina win the 2024 Copa América, believes there should be no pressure on his longtime teammate to step away.Speaking to TNT Sports, Di María said Messi alone should decide when his international career comes to an end."Yes, Leo should continue for as long as he wants," Di María said."I think he can keep going for many more years."The former Real Madrid, Paris Saint-Germain and Benfica winger argued that Messi's performances throughout the World Cup proved age has done little to diminish his influence."At 39 years old, he's proven he's one of the best and still the best in history, with no ceiling."Although Argentina ultimately fell short in the final, Messi once again carried much of the creative burden for Lionel Scaloni's side during the tournament.He finished the World Cup with eight goals and four assists, leading Argentina back to a second consecutive final after inspiring several decisive performances throughout the knockout rounds.Argentina's title defence came to an end after Torres capitalised in the second period of extra time, shortly after Enzo Fernández had been sent off in stoppage time of normal time following a second yellow card.Reduced to 10 men, Argentina were unable to find an equaliser as Spain's control of possession eventually translated into the goal that settled the final.Despite the disappointment, Di María believes the campaign should be remembered for much more than the defeat in New Jersey.He singled out Argentina's dramatic 2-1 semi-final victory over England as one of the defining moments of the tournament."The win over England was a great joy for all of Argentina, and this was clear and made me very happy," he said."I am grateful to everyone in the Argentina squad forever."Reflecting on the team's journey, Di María praised the resilience shown by Scaloni's players throughout the competition."I suffered in every match, but the players found the strength within themselves and it led them to victories.""Sometimes you win finals and sometimes luck is not on your side, but they raised the name of the national team high."The 38-year-old even suggested that, emotionally, Argentina had already delivered a lasting memory before reaching the final."For me, the World Cup ended when Argentina beat England," he said. "They gave the country an indescribable joy."Messi is not the only senior figure whose future has come under discussion following the tournament.Speculation has also surrounded head coach Lionel Scaloni after Argentina narrowly missed out on back-to-back World Cup titles, but Di María hopes the manager remains in charge to guide the next generation."I hope he continues for everyone's benefit, as there is a good generation of young players seeking glory," Di María said."He will know what he wants, but I hope he stays."Argentina's squad still features a blend of experienced leaders and emerging talent capable of competing for future honours, making continuity an attractive option as preparations eventually begin for the next major international cycle.Messi has largely stayed out of the spotlight since the final defeat and has not publicly addressed whether he intends to continue playing for Argentina.His immediate focus is expected to shift back to club football with Inter Miami as the MLS season resumes, while another World Cup appears highly unlikely given his age.The 2028 Copa América, however, remains a realistic possibility should Messi decide to extend his international career.For Di María, the message is simple: as long as Messi continues producing performances like those seen throughout the 2026 World Cup, there is no reason to place an artificial deadline on one of the greatest international careers football has ever seen.
Article Summary: Argentina lost 1-0 to Spain in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final in New Jersey. The defeat ended Argentina's hopes of retaining the trophy they won in Qatar four years earlier. Spain claimed their second men's World Cup title after substitute Ferran Torres scored the decisive goal in the 106th minute. Lionel Messi has yet to confirm whether he intends to continue playing for Argentina.

Article Title: "A lot of this was purposefully done to embarrass Ryan Clark": New explosive claim hints at a deeper story behind Ryan Clark's ESPN firing
Article Text:
New explosive claim hints at a deeper story behind Ryan Clark's ESPN firing(Getty Images)

New comments raise fresh questions about how Ryan Clark left ESPN

Ryan Clark's exit from ESPN is no longer just another layoff story. Days after the network parted ways with the former NFL safety, fresh comments on national television have sparked a new debate. While ESPN has called the cuts part of a broader business move, one media voice believes there may have been more behind how Clark's departure played out.Clark spent more than 10 years at ESPN after retiring from the NFL. He became one of the network's most familiar football analysts. Now, the way he left the company has become just as big a story as the layoff itself.Ryan Clark was one of several well-known names let go during ESPN's latest round of layoffs.Karl Ravech, Tom Pelissero, Andreas Hale and Cam Newton were also among those affected. Reports said Clark found out about the decision during a break while filming “NFL Live”. Clark later claimed ESPN told him then because another outlet was about to report the news.The story took another turn during CNN This Morning. Jason "Jah" Lee, senior editor at Bossip and a CNN contributor, questioned whether everything happened by chance.He said, "I think Ryan Clark got swept up in some level of culture war retribution. The reason he got fired during the segment is because an outlet called OutKick contacted ESPN threatening to leak this information. How would OutKick get this information?"Lee then made another strong claim. He said, "If you know Clay Travis, he is not a bleeding-heart liberal. I feel a lot of this was purposefully done to embarrass Ryan Clark."His shocking remark quickly drew a lot of attention online and sparked debate across the sports media world. Some people agreed with him, while others felt ESPN's decision was simply part of another round of cost-cutting. ESPN has not responded to Lee's remarks.Plus, Former boxing champion and ESPN analyst Tim Bradley saw things differently. Speaking about Clark's emotional reaction to losing his job, Bradley said the television business can change overnight. He said, "You gotta understand this industry is like that. You don't know that? How long you been in this industry? It's like that. You here one minute, gone the next."Bradley also said money usually drives these decisions. "It's all about numbers. That's all it's about. It's about numbers."Ryan Clark joined ESPN in 2015 and became a regular face on NFL Live, First Take and Get Up. He also built a strong following through The Pivot Podcast.ESPN has said the layoffs are part of wider business changes as it moves closer to integrating with NFL Media after Disney's new agreement. Even so, Ryan Clark's exit continues to draw attention, with many still asking whether this was just another layoff or a story that goes much deeper.
Article Summary: Ryan Clark was one of several well-known names let go during ESPN's latest round of layoffs. Reports said Clark found out about the decision during a break while filming “NFL Live” Clark later claimed ESPN told him then because another outlet was about to report the news. ESPN has said the layoffs are part of wider business changes.

Article Title: Who is Daniel Adongo? Former NFL player and first Kenyan in the league deported from the US to Kenya by ICE
Article Text:

Who is Daniel Adongo? The first Kenyan to ever play in the NFL



Why was Daniel Adongo deported?



Daniel Adongo made history back in 2013 as the first Kenyan to ever play in the NFL , arriving with zero football experience and an unusual backstory rooted in professional rugby. Now, more than a decade later, he's back in the news for a very different reason: U.S. immigration officials have deported him to Kenya after years of legal trouble following the end of his brief NFL career. Here's who he is, what led to the deportation, and what happens next.Adongo, now 37, was born in Nairobi and moved to South Africa as a teenager to join a rugby academy, going on to play professional rugby in South Africa and New Zealand between 2011 and 2013.The Indianapolis Colts signed him that same year as a raw athletic project, a 6-foot-5, 270-pound convert with elite size but no football background, something the team openly called an "experiment."He spent two seasons with the franchise, appearing in just five career games mostly on special teams, before being released in 2015 following a police welfare check at a home he shared with a woman in Fishers, Indiana. No charges came from that specific incident, but it appears to have factored into his exit from the team.Adongo overstayed his visa in 2016, a year after his NFL career ended, and remained in the U.S. for nearly a decade.During that stretch, Indiana law enforcement arrested him multiple times on charges including felony intimidation, battery, and disorderly conduct, and he was ultimately convicted of criminal mischief with damage in 2020, drawing a 364-day jail sentence.A Department of Justice immigration judge ordered his removal in March 2026, and he was detained without bond under the Laken Riley Act, a federal law requiring mandatory detention for undocumented immigrants convicted of certain crimes. ICE carried out the deportation from Chicago on June 20, 2026.ICE has framed the case as proof that no one, including former professional athletes, is exempt from immigration enforcement. Separately, NBC News reports that Adongo's family and attorneys have raised concerns about his mental state and a possible brain injury, questions that the Department of Homeland Security has not yet addressed. For now, Adongo's NFL story brief, unusual and historic, ends with him back in the country he left as a teenage rugby prospect nearly two decades ago.
Article Summary: Daniel Adongo was born in Nairobi and moved to South Africa as a teenager to join a rugby academy. He went on to play professional rugby in South Africa and New Zealand between 2011 and 2013. The Indianapolis Colts signed him that same year as a raw athletic project with elite size but no football background.
